scope: Different-author source-only review. No license query, VCS, simulation, SAIF generation, PrimeTime PX, production attempt, result or release was run or created.

p1.finding: The author checker scans the current execution sources, but the production runner never traverses and exact-checks the six direct simulation/control members recorded by the exact M1684 source contract: the assertion module, wrapper, UCLI Tcl, PTPX Tcl, and two VCS filelists. Pinning the M1684 contract file itself does not transitively pin its members.
p1.impact: Any of those files can drift after M1699 and before the one future attempt. The runner would still pass authority/predecessor checks and could compile or execute changed control logic, including an injected force, so the claimed active-force ban and exact five-case campaign are not fail-closed at production time.
p1.required_repair: Before lock admission and again before attempt consumption, parse the exact M1684 source contract and exact-check every listed execution member against its recorded SHA, or copy those member hashes into a runner-enforced immutable inventory. The check must occur in the launch-capable runner, not only in the author checker.

p1.finding: M1686 is absent now, but the launch-capable runner has no M1686 path and no os.path.lexists gate. Only the author checker performs `not M1686.exists()` during source review.
p1.impact: An unauthorized M1686 regular file or dangling symlink can appear after this review without stopping M1698. That does not replace M1700 authority, but it violates the explicit permanent-denial invariant and leaves two contradictory launch artifacts in the same chain.
p1.required_repair: Define the exact forbidden M1686 namespace in the runner and reject os.path.lexists(M1686), its digest sidecar, and its outer-seal sidecar before attempt consumption; the future release author must enforce the same absence gate.

p2.finding: The Tcl branch of active_force_present matches force only at the beginning of a non-comment line. The active command `if {1} { force dut/q 0 }` is accepted as clean by the checker.
p2.disposition: Replace the line-start regex with a conservative Tcl command/token scan that recognizes force after command separators and inside active brace bodies. Add inline, semicolon and commented/string mutation tests. Exact runtime source binding remains the release-blocking repair.

single_next_action: Create a newly numbered additive successor that runtime-binds all exact execution sources, enforces M1686 absence with lexists, and fixes inline Tcl force detection; then submit it for a fresh different-author hammer. Do not author M1700 against M1698.
